Reading the entire request and response bodies.
Generating, for example, an MD5 hash from the request and response bodies and logging it.

During Gateway startup, retrieving data from an external service, loading it and storing it in memory. Then periodically (e.g. every 15 minutes) calling that service and updating the in-memory data. If communication fails, the last successfully stored value must remain in memory.
Until the data has been successfully retrieved from the external service and loaded into memory, the Gateway must return OUT_OF_SERVICE in its health check.

Compliance with the OWASP API Security Top 10
API2: Broken Authentication

Ability to secure endpoints and define different authentication requirements for different endpoints, using Basic Authentication, OAuth2/OIDC (e.g. Entra ID) JWT, mTLS. For example a policy validating JWT signature (JWKS), issuer, audience, token validity dates.
Brute-force protection: rate limiting (by API key, user or OAuth token), spike arrest / throttling, monitoring and alerting (SIEM integration).
API4: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
Per-service size limits: sending a file or payload that exceeds the permitted limit.
Per-service JSON threat protection: maximum nesting depth, number of fields, number of array elements, value length.
Per-service XML threat protection: number of elements, attributes, entities.

Rate limiting / quota per API, endpoint and business operation; validation of parameters affecting backend load (limit, pageSize, depth), ability to block or override parameter values through a policy.
API6: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
Control access to selected endpoints, methods or properties using request sequence control, blocking automated requests (headless browser), CAPTCHA, detection of non-human behaviour.
API7: Server-Side Request Forgery
Detection of attempted SSRF requests, e.g. requests targeting 169.254.169.254, localhost or 127.0.0.1.
API8: Security Misconfiguration
Enforcing TLS versions and cipher suites.
HTTP method filtering: allowed GET, POST; blocked PUT, DELETE, TRACE; return 405.
CORS enforcement: central CORS policy configuration, policy inheritance.
Security headers: Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy.
Content-Type restrictions: allowed content types, reject disallowed with 415.
Header transformation: remove Server and X-Powered-By, add standard security headers.
Error response sanitization: hide stack traces, technologies, hostnames and private IPs; standardized error messages.
API9: Improper Inventory Management
API inventory: unknown APIs, old versions, shadow APIs, zombie APIs, endpoints outside the API management process.
API versioning: version identification, deprecation, lifecycle management.
API usage visibility: consumers, activity by version, unused APIs.
